findings.section: Wave 9 — W9 — Auth Enforce + Cookie Navigation + Ops Cutover (C2 gate)
findings.message: When ANCHOR_TOKEN is rotated, the iPhone PWA's installed start URL containing the old token becomes invalid. Because the server returns a 401 with no login/token entry form, the PWA is completely stranded with no way to re-authenticate other than deleting it from the home screen and re-adding it. This creates a highly frustrated UX for daily mobile use.

findings.section: Wave 17 — W17 — C4 Live Demo + ConPTY Verdict Application
findings.message: If the ConPTY spike yields a NO verdict, PTYs remain dashboard-owned. While the 'drain' can capture documents and seed a warm-resume, the actual running OS processes (like active SSH sessions, REPLs, or running builds) inside the PTY will be terminated during an NSSM restart. Claiming this does not cost 'live terminal context' is misleading and hides a disruptive UX regression.

findings.section: Wave 16 — W16 — External Supervisor Service + Live Probes
findings.message: Persisting tail cursors directly to the job directory on every read/write creates a high risk of Windows file sharing violations (EACCES) when the dashboard reads and the supervisor writes concurrently. Under heavy log output, this contention will cause UI stalls or stream failures, breaking John's daily dashboard experience.

findings.section: Wave 12 — W12 — journal.py Core: emit() Choke Point + Three-Marker Lifecycle + Butler Envelope
findings.message: The startup reconciler lacks a concurrency lease or grace period for active writes. If a legacy write takes longer to complete, a concurrent reconciler run or health check will see the legacy write as missing and prematurely append an ABORTED marker. When the active write subsequently succeeds and tries to append CONFIRM, the journal stream will be corrupted with conflicting markers.

If a crash occurs during the legacy-store write, the legacy file (e.g., `index.json`) may be left in a torn or corrupted state, causing the verify-against-legacy predicate to either crash or report 'not landed' (auto-abort). Because the reconciler appends ABORTED, the event payload in the INTENT is discarded and excluded from `rebuild_index.py` (which only processes CONFIRMED events). The operator is left with a corrupt index.json and no automated way to recover the lost data from the journal, violating the North Star requirement that the 'lost from an index' bug class be recoverable-by-construction.

findings.criterion: 2. One route table, declarative auth, default-deny.
findings.message: When John rotates the ANCHOR_TOKEN, the hardcoded token in the installed iPhone PWA's start URL (`/auth?token=<old_token>&next=/`) becomes invalid. Since the start URL of an installed PWA is fixed at install time, the PWA will fail to authenticate on launch, forcing John to manually delete and re-install the PWA every time he rotates the token. This creates a high-friction operator recovery path that contradicts the state machine's goal of unattended phone bootstrapping.

If a job exits during the supervisor's restart window, the supervisor cannot acquire a process handle on boot and will execute the fallback liveness poll, marking the job terminal with the exit code as 'honestly unknown'. Since the child does not persist its own exit status to its job directory, the operator/dashboard loses the true exit status of any job completing during a service restart, breaking the automation logic for the Butler substrate.

findings.criterion: 6. Runtime state out of the repo.
findings.message: The proposed Step-A rollback path ('stop service -> repoint ANCHOR_DATA_DIR at the untouched original dir -> start -> healthcheck') assumes the original directory remains untouched. However, if the migrated service runs for any period of time before a rollback is triggered, John will lose all new tasks, project updates, and session records created in the relocated directory during that window. A safe rollback must include a data-reconciliation or reverse-migration step to prevent silent operator data loss.

While W2 introduces a contract-versioning shim that checks the build ID on `_postJson` calls and returns 409, it does not mandate this check for WebSocket upgrade requests (`term_ws`). A stale browser tab could successfully upgrade and establish a WebSocket connection to a newly deployed server, bypassing the build ID check. This allows mismatched frontend-backend code to run over terminal sessions, risking state corruption or UI crashes during active use.

findings.criterion: 6. Runtime state out of the repo.
findings.message: Performing `git rm --cached` leaves the physical runtime files on disk in the repository directory. If any code path incorrectly falls back to the repository paths, the tests and healthchecks will pass because the files are still physically present, masking path-resolution bugs that would break a fresh clone. The files must be physically removed or renamed in the repo directory during the hygiene gate to verify complete separation.

The plan mandates a 'numeric complexity/effort budget threshold' in W3 to mechanically select the W17 PTY-adoption branch, but it does not define the units or methodology for measuring this complexity (e.g., developer hours, lines of prototype code, or API call counts). Without a defined metric, the threshold cannot be objectively applied at the W17 gate, risking subjective debates and delaying the branch decision.

When the supervisor restarts, all open pipe handles (including the stdin pipe redirected to the job) are closed by the OS. The running job's stdin will receive an EOF immediately. It is impossible for the restarted supervisor to write to the stdin of a re-adopted job, meaning any pending or future AskUserQuestion prompt for that job will fail.

Rotating the ANCHOR_TOKEN will break the installed iPhone PWA because its start URL is fixed at installation time on iOS. A PWA launch after rotation will present the old token, failing authentication with no way for the phone to automatically update its start URL, forcing a manual deletion and re-adding of the PWA.

Running the reconciler 'on demand' on a live service can cause race conditions. An active, in-flight mutation that has appended an INTENT but not yet completed its legacy write or CONFIRM could be falsely aborted or confirmed by the reconciler. The reconciler must either run only when the engine is quiescent (e.g. strict startup boot phase) or exclude intents younger than a safety tail window.

The script install_supervisor.ps1 attempts to set the NSSM service ObjectName to a custom user account (.\john) without prompting for or storing a password. On Windows, service configuration for custom user accounts requires a password; without it, the service will fail to install or fail to start with a logon error.

The Step-A rollback plan claims 'no data reconstruction, because the original dir was never mutated.' However, if the rollback is executed after the migrated service has run and accepted new user mutations, reverting to the original directory will cause data loss of all mutations made post-migration.
